title: Non-resident inspection costs and the plan of correction after a cited violation
subtopic: Inspection costs and plans of correction
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.24(2) all costs associated with inspections of non-resident pharmacies shall be paid by the non-resident pharmacy or applicant. Under 247 CMR 9.25(1) a pharmacy shall submit to the Board a written plan of correction for each violation cited in a statement of deficiency or inspection report within 21 days or in the timeframe directed by the Board, prepared and submitted in the manner and format specified by the Board. Under 9.25(2) the plan describes the corrective action in response to each cited violation, the expected completion or implementation date, and the individual or individuals responsible for each action. Under 9.25(3) the Manager of Record, and the licensee who supervises the Manager of Record's practice of pharmacy if applicable, shall sign the plan. Under 9.25(4) a pharmacy shall achieve compliance with the laws and regulations governing the practice of pharmacy in the most expeditious manner possible. Under 9.25(5) a plan that does not meet the requirements of the relevant 247 CMR section shall be considered unacceptable by the Board and returned to the pharmacy, and the pharmacy shall submit a revised plan within seven days. The self-inspection requirement in 247 CMR 9.19(21) is not among the 9.19 provisions that 9.19(23) disapplies for non-resident pharmacies or that 9.19(24) disapplies for institutional sterile compounding pharmacies.
exam_relevance: Tests the two clocks that follow a cited deficiency, who signs the plan, and who pays for a non-resident inspection.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

numeric_facts.fact: Plan of correction for each cited violation
numeric_facts.conditions: or in the timeframe directed by the Board

numeric_facts.fact: Revised plan after an unacceptable plan is returned

exceptions: The Board may direct a timeframe other than 21 days for the plan of correction.
common_confusions: A plan is owed for each violation cited in a statement of deficiency or inspection report, not only for the most serious one.
The 21-day and seven-day periods are separate: the second runs only after the Board returns an unacceptable plan.
verification_notes: Read in the Board's publication of 247 CMR 9.00 (PDF, pages dated 12/6/24) on mass.gov on 2026-09-17.
